book.title: Feel the Fear and Do It Anyway
book.author: Susan Jeffers

confidence_note: The reference TR text says Jeffers decided to go skydiving after a friend did, and drew the book's thesis from the jump. That story cannot be verified in the book and is left out. The book's core content is well established: Jeffers describes 'Five Truths About Fear', including that the fear will never go away as long as you continue to grow; that the only way to get rid of the fear of doing something is to go out and do it; that everyone feels fear when on unfamiliar territory; and that pushing through fear is less frightening than living with the underlying fear that comes from a feeling of helplessness. She also traces most fears to one core fear: 'I can't handle it.' The book grew out of a course she taught on fear.
facts: Jeffers argues that at the bottom of every fear is one simple belief: 'I can't handle it.'
She lists five truths about fear.
One: the fear will never go away as long as I continue to grow.
Two: the only way to get rid of the fear of doing something is to go out and do it.
Three: the only way to feel better about myself is to go out and do it.
Four: not only am I going to experience fear whenever I'm on unfamiliar territory, but so is everyone else.
Five: pushing through fear is less frightening than living with the underlying fear that comes from a feeling of helplessness.
Her message is not to wait for fear to disappear, but to build trust that you can handle whatever happens.
tension: Most people wait to feel ready before they act. Jeffers says that moment never comes.
opening_idea: Many people are waiting for the day they stop feeling afraid. Jeffers's first truth is that it won't come.

lessons.idea: Fear accompanies growth; waiting for it to vanish means waiting forever.

reflect: What are you waiting to feel ready for?
What would change if you believed 'I'll handle it'?
reflect_final: What would you do this month if you accepted that the fear will come along?

use_cases.situation: You keep postponing a career change until you feel ready.
use_cases.move: Take one small real step this week while the fear is still there.

use_cases.situation: A friend is anxious about a new role and thinks they're alone in it.
use_cases.move: Share that everyone feels fear on unfamiliar ground.

use_cases.situation: A team member avoids presenting because they're nervous.
use_cases.move: Remind them the fear won't go away first; offer a short, low-stakes first presentation.

pocket_idea: Don't wait for fear to leave; trust that you'll handle it, and go.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Fear never goes away as long as you keep growing.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: 'I can't handle it' and the five truths about fear.
conversation_variants.question_idea: What are you waiting to feel ready for?
